title: Engineered allogeneic T cells decoupling T-cell-receptor and CD3 signalling enhance the antitumour activity of bispecific antibodies
source: Kapetanovic et al., show notes as published
one_line: Mutating a conserved FGxGT motif in the TCR alpha chain uncouples antigen recognition from CD3 signalling, yielding allogeneic 'AED' T cells that ignore their native antigen but can still be redirected by bispecific antibodies such as blinatumomab.
key_claims: Mutation of the conserved FGxGT motif in the TCR alpha constant region disrupts transmission of antigen recognition into downstream CD3 activation while leaving the receptor otherwise intact.
In vitro, AED T cells showed reduced proliferation, cytokine release and cytotoxicity against their native (allo)antigen.
AED T cells retained normal activation and tumour killing when engaged via CD3 by blinatumomab in the presence of CD19+ tumour cells.
In a mouse model, AED T cells plus blinatumomab eliminated CD19+ tumours without signs of alloreactivity, whereas control allogeneic T cells showed alloreactivity.
The approach is positioned as an enabler of off-the-shelf allogeneic T cell products combined with bispecific antibodies, avoiding reliance on compromised patient T cells.
limitations: No quantitative values (proliferation, cytokine, killing magnitudes) reported in the available material.
Host-versus-graft rejection of the donor AED T cells was not addressed.
Demonstration limited to blinatumomab/CD19 in a mouse model; other bispecific antibodies and tumour types untested.
Long-term safety, persistence and efficacy in humans not evaluated.
Residual antigen responsiveness and whether the FGxGT mutation is the optimal decoupling edit were not resolved.
open_questions: Does the AED design prevent GvHD in a human clinical trial while preserving biAb-driven efficacy?
How durable is the decoupling — can AED T cells regain alloreactive signalling over time or under strong stimulation?
Does the approach generalise across other bispecific antibody formats and solid tumour targets?
Can AED T cells be protected from host immune rejection to allow persistence?
